The type conversions dazdiff will make

Source: R/types.R
cast_rules.Rd

In mode = "benchmark", diff_table() casts each column of the candidate to the type it has in the benchmark. These are the conversions it will attempt and the ones it refuses. A conversion that would need a guess – a number read as a flag, a factor's integer codes read as values – is refused rather than made.

Usage

cast_rules(wide = TRUE)

Arguments

wide

If TRUE (the default), a grid of source types by target types, with "yes" for an allowed conversion, "-" for a refused one and "=" where source and target are the same type. If FALSE, one row per pair, with each rule's note.

Value

A data.table.

Details

A cast that drops the fraction of a value (a double to an integer, a timestamp to its calendar day, a Date holding part of a day to its text) is a truncation: it is made when truncate = TRUE, which is the default, and refused otherwise.

Text is parsed strictly: anything that is not a number, a logical literal or a date in date_format is refused, and that includes the text "NA", since a missing value has to arrive as NA. "NaN" and "Inf" are numbers. A double written as text is written in fixed notation, so 100000 becomes "100000", not "1e+05". A timestamp written as text is its local time in its own timezone, which the text does not record, always as "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S" (midnight included), followed by the fraction of a second to the microsecond when it has one, as in "2024-01-01 10:00:00.25". An integer64 column (from bit64) becomes a double when that is exact, an integer within range, or its decimal text.

A logical column becomes a Date only when every value is NA: that is how readers such as read.csv() and data.table::fread() type a column with no values, and the Date column it stands for is then all NA as well.

Examples

cast_rules()
#>         from character logical   Date numeric integer
#>       <char>    <char>  <char> <char>  <char>  <char>
#> 1: character         =     yes    yes     yes     yes
#> 2:   logical       yes       =      -     yes     yes
#> 3:      Date       yes       -      =     yes     yes
#> 4:   numeric       yes       -    yes       =     yes
#> 5:   integer       yes       -    yes     yes       =
#> 6:   POSIXct       yes       -    yes     yes     yes
#> 7:    factor       yes       -      -       -       -
#> 8: integer64       yes       -      -     yes     yes
cast_rules(wide = FALSE)
#>          from        to allowed
#>        <char>    <char>  <lgcl>
#>  1: character   logical    TRUE
#>  2: character      Date    TRUE
#>  3: character   numeric    TRUE
#>  4: character   integer    TRUE
#>  5:   logical character    TRUE

#>  7:   logical   numeric    TRUE
#>  8:   logical   integer    TRUE
#>  9:      Date character    TRUE
#> 10:      Date   logical   FALSE
#> 11:      Date   numeric    TRUE
#> 12:      Date   integer    TRUE
#> 13:   numeric character    TRUE
#> 14:   numeric   logical   FALSE
#> 15:   numeric      Date    TRUE
#> 16:   numeric   integer    TRUE
#> 17:   integer character    TRUE
#> 18:   integer   logical   FALSE
#> 19:   integer      Date    TRUE
#> 20:   integer   numeric    TRUE
#> 21:   POSIXct character    TRUE
#> 22:   POSIXct   logical   FALSE
#> 23:   POSIXct      Date    TRUE
#> 24:   POSIXct   numeric    TRUE
#> 25:   POSIXct   integer    TRUE
#> 26:    factor character    TRUE
#> 27:    factor   logical   FALSE
#> 28:    factor      Date   FALSE
#> 29:    factor   numeric   FALSE
#> 30:    factor   integer   FALSE
#> 31: integer64 character    TRUE
#> 32: integer64   logical   FALSE
#> 33: integer64      Date   FALSE
#> 34: integer64   numeric    TRUE

#>  3:                                                                                                                                                                                                                        parsed from the text; a missing value must be NA, not the text "NA"
